title: Specified finite and tower composite orientation arrow data
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, composable quasi-compact compactifiable scheme morphisms $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$, and chosen open/proper factorizations of $f,g,h=gf$. Use the strict ordinary tower operations, ordered shifted Tate lines and specified diagonal purity data of [def-sp-tower-gamma-data], and the given adjunction pairs of [def-sp-adjoint-compositor-data]. Define $\omega_g=G_g A_Z$ in the uniform constructible tower category and $\rho=t_{f,\omega_g}$. For a supplied exceptional compositor $c:G_h\simeq G_fG_g$ and a proof that $\rho$ is invertible, define $\mu=c_1$ followed by $\rho^{-1}$. At a finite coefficient ring $A$, define the canonical exceptional compositor as the unique right-adjoint comparison of the proper/open compact-support compositor, the tensor mate and $\rho_A,\mu_A$ by the same counit construction, using the ordinary finite maps and ordered Tate lines of [def-pur-finite-smooth-canonical-maps]. Define the shifted-Tate splitting $L_h\simeq f^*L_g\otimes L_f$ recursively by the canonical coefficient pullback comparison, unitors and tensor associator, including the zero-dimensional cases. For a supplied tower splitting, define TowerSplitNormalized to assert that its finite comparison square is this finite splitting, using the normalized root, coefficient, pullback and tensor words of [def-sp-p1-level-words]. These are definitions of specified arrows and their finite normalization predicate, not a composition-equality or existence assertion.
